package.title: ServiceNow Q2 2026 earnings forecast — first-principles OFF model

scenarios.label: Bear case
scenarios.description: Lower core growth, weaker FX, and integration pressure on margin.

scenarios.label: Base case
scenarios.description: Revenue near the company guide, reported cRPO 50 bps above reported guidance but in line with constant-currency guidance, and operating margin above guide.

scenarios.label: Bull case
scenarios.description: Stronger core growth, partial delayed-deal recovery, and operating leverage.

outputs.label: Bear Subscription revenue
outputs.methodology: Prior-year Q2 subscription revenue grown by scenario core growth, disclosed Armis contribution, FX, and delayed-deal catch-up.

outputs.label: Bear Total revenue
outputs.methodology: Scenario subscription revenue plus separately forecast professional services and other revenue.

outputs.label: Bear Reported cRPO growth
outputs.methodology: Independent scenario judgment shown against both reported and constant-currency company guidance; it is not a bookings, cohort, or contract-duration bridge.

outputs.label: Bear Non-GAAP operating margin

outputs.label: Bear Non-GAAP diluted EPS

attestations.materialityPolicy: All reported operating baselines, disclosed acquisition contribution, diluted-share input, and analyst assumptions that materially drive the five base-case headline outputs are declared; scenario outputs use the same policy.
attestations.scope: The five base-case Q2 2026 headline outputs produced by the ServiceNow earnings workbook as of 2026-07-22.
knownExclusions: Consensus revenue and EPS are comparison-only and have no forecast lineage.
The model has no event-isolating options, positioning, or share-price reaction inputs.
Reported cRPO is an independent scenario judgment, not a bookings, renewal, cohort, or contract-duration model; Armis contract terms limit associated cRPO recognition.
Non-GAAP EPS uses an operating-to-net-income conversion ratio rather than a full tax and below-the-line schedule.
Source URLs are live public pages and are not independently archived inside the package.
Lineage is author-declared and has not been independently verified.
The package does not claim cross-engine spreadsheet execution equivalence.
